text:
Tara (product): quick sync 1: Private setup wizard network step 1 user tests say the page feels scary. lots of red and long paragraphs. ideas to make it calmer?

Eli (design): shorter status lines, friendlier verbs ('Looks good' instead of 'Pass'), and hide advanced rules under 'More details'. show a single-line explanation per rule.

Noah (frontend): agree. implement as status list with left icon, middle label + one-liner, right actions. on mobile stack the columns. ensure tab order hits actions last.

June (a11y): don't rely on color. include visible text status and an aria-live region so screen readers announce changes like 'Outbound 443 check failed'. add a skip link to jump to failures.

Kai (pm): copy note: add a short bold reassurance near top: 'We only run read-only checks from your agent; we will not modify your firewall.' keeps legal teams happy.

Eli (design): microcopy suggestions: Retry -> 'Re-run check'; Details -> 'Why this matters'. keep it non-technical.

Noah (frontend): for the Details panel include a small collapsible code snippet for ops, hidden by default, e.g. `curl -I https://api.redwood.ai/health`. provide a 'Copy' button with aria-live confirmation.

June (a11y): code block should be a region with aria-label='Diagnostic command'. test with VoiceOver + NVDA and keyboard-only navigation.

Tara (product): decision: 1) compact one-line statuses, 2) advanced rules collapsed, 3) top reassurance copy, 4) aria-live + skip link, 5) mobile stacking. anyone object?

Eli (design): yay, will update figma and supply token names.

Noah (frontend): yay, will open feature branch and prototype focus behaviour.

June (a11y): yay, I'll write the QA checklist and example SR reads.

Kai (pm): added to sprint board and flagged urgent for Private onboarding flow.
